Setup (per docs/research/variance_of_associator.md § "Worked example:
single Fano generator"):
A(a, b, c) := ‖[a, b, c]‖²   where [a,b,c] = (a·b)·c − a·(b·c)
Unperturbed: [a,b,c] = 2·e_7, A = 4.

variance (from the β document, derivation):
Var(A) ≈ 64 σ²                                (TRUTH)
If the current compiler's stepwise scalar-product rule were applied
instead, it would give:
Var_compiler(A) ≈ 16 σ²                       (COMPILER, 4× low)
This test computes the sample variance of A over N = 100,000 Monte
Carlo samples and compares to the TRUTH formula. It does NOT test the
compiler's variance_of() — that requires the full Knowledge<f64>
chain which introduces unrelated complexities (see ζ buffer bug). The
compiler comparison is deferred to a separate test.
Pass criterion: |MC_var − 64σ²| / 64σ² < 0.05 (5% relative error).
If this passes, β's analytical formula is validated empirically. The
remaining claim — that the compiler produces 16σ² — is then a
separate reading-confirmation task.

Reads the committed benchmark CSV benchmarks/pbpk/model_form_uc.csv at
runtime (read_file, no embedded data) and aggregates the model-form

robust to the aggregation choice:
METHOD 1 — AUC-weighted residual fraction
Per organ:  resid1_o = |AUC28_o - AUC14_o| / AUC28_o
where AUC_o = trapezoidal integral of C_o(t) over the sample times.
Aggregate scalar (exposure-weighted across organs):
resid1 = Σ_o |AUC28_o - AUC14_o| / Σ_o AUC28_o
The 28-compartment model is the truth reference (denominator).
METHOD 2 — Peak-window residual fraction (t ≤ 6 h)
Restrict to the early/peak window where absolute exposure is highest.
Exposure-weighted (concentration-mass-weighted) relative delta:
resid2 = Σ_{t≤6h,o} |C28 - C14| / Σ_{t≤6h,o} C28
NEAR-ZERO-TAIL GUARD: the CSV's delta_pct hits 1246% at the brain
t=30h sample where C28 ≈ 1e-6. Because BOTH methods weight by absolute
exposure (AUC magnitude / concentration mass), that late-time tail is
negligible in the numerator AND denominator and CANNOT dominate. We do
NOT use the raw delta_pct column for the residual fraction.

form discrepancy, so they are NOT summed (that double-counts one source);

Existing run-pass `knowledge_octonion_structure.sio` carries uncertainty on

What it proves about the compiler today:
1. Parser accepts `Knowledge<Octonion>` (struct as inner type, not just f64/i64).
2. Type-checker accepts the `Knowledge { value: octonion_literal }` construction.
3. `.value` projection through a struct inner returns the struct.

that does the algebra on the underlying `Octonion` (not on the Knowledge
capsule directly) lowers to ELF and runs.
What it does NOT claim: arithmetic operators (+ - * /) on `Knowledge<Octonion>`
directly — the codegen at lean_single.sio:6796 legitimately rejects struct
inner types for those operators because GUM variance propagation requires a

argument, and checks the callee receives the exact content -- not just

env-φ finding): `var x = measure(1); if c { x = measure(2) }; use(x)`
must NOT let x's post-if type revert to measure(1)'s narrow set. The bug
was structural, not just "wrong branch wins": checker_check_block_inplace
push_scope()s/pop_scope()s around every block including if-arms, and
pop_scope discards ANY env rebind made inside -- so the reassignment
literally never reached anywhere outside the branch, AS IF it had not
happened. checker_merge_ns_reassigned_inplace (called at the if/match
merge point) closes this: reassigning a Knowledge var while
ns_branch_depth > 0 records the name instead of a rebind that would just
be discarded, and the merge re-binds it in the NOW-RESTORED outer scope
with noise_set_id forced to top.
The observable proof is NOT just the "env_join" trace line at the merge
(that only proves the merge RAN) -- it's reading x again afterward: `x +
w3` unions x's POST-merge type with an empty set, so its own "union=-1"
line is the end-to-end proof that the forced-top value actually survived
past the if-statement into the code that follows it.
Per-rule sabotage: SOUNIO_NS_SABOTAGE_JOIN=1 disables the env-merge
(same knob as the CFG-join fixes), reproducing the pre-fix bug: x reverts
to its PRE-if handle, and the trailing union's handle becomes a real
(non-top) combination of that stale handle with w3's empty set instead
of -1 -- proving the env-join, not something else, closed the hole.

comments: requires: madaros because IR_MAX_INSTRS is a Madaros IR limit. lean_single --
which the CI full-test-suite runs -- has no such wall and compiles this file
happily, so without the guard this is a false red. That is exactly how it
failed the first time it was pushed.
#1645: a function past IR_MAX_INSTRS had its remaining instructions DROPPED and
the compile still exited 0, writing a binary whose tail was simply missing. The
program ran, printed nothing after the cut, and exited 0 as well -- the "empty
green" shape reported in #1586 on a ~1190-line main.
Why it survived: Lowerer is threaded by VALUE. `emit` writes the instruction
through a Box, so the truncation is permanent and visible in the finished
module, but `had_error` is a plain scalar field of the Lowerer value -- any link
in the lowering chain that discards the Lowerer it was handed loses the flag
while keeping the damage. Measured: instr_count pinned at exactly 4096 and
had_error FALSE, so all six `if body_result.had_error` checks passed.
The fix records the wall somewhere value semantics cannot reach and ORs it into
every IrLowerResult at construction, so the existing consumers work unchanged.
This file must stay ONE function: the wall is per function, so splitting it
across helpers is exactly the workaround that hid the defect.
~330 statements of this shape lower to more than 4096 IR instructions.

comments: A refinement must hold at the RETURN, not only at a binding.
This is the Madaros half of a measured engine divergence. On main@88c2ab8ee8
the *mut checker spine calls checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace from
exactly two places (check.sio:9627, 9687), both in the let/var handlers, and
check/compat.sio never looks at refinement_id. So under Madaros a refinement
is enforced where a value is BOUND and nowhere else:
$ artifacts/madaros --check tests/compile-fail/refinement_f64_return_violation.sio
check: OK
lean_single rejects the same file. tests/known_failures/
hardened_diagnostics_full_suite.txt records the split in its own words
(2026-08-23): "default Madaros still answers `check: OK` on that file, so the
refinement is unenforced there; that is a compiler defect, not a manifest
one." This test is that defect, pinned for the integer case.
SCOPE. checker_check_refinement_literal_inplace only fires when
last_literal_kind is 1 (int) or 2 (float), so this pins the LITERAL return.
The propagated case is a separate, still-open hole:
fn lift(x: i64) -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { x }        // still accepted
fn f() -> { n: i64 | n >= 0 } { let b = 0 - 7  return b }  // still accepted
Those need dataflow the checker does not have here; main's own
tests/compile-fail/refinement_return_var.sio pins that case for lean_single
and is untouched by this test. Closing the literal case is what the
known-failures manifest asks for, and is where the fix stops.
The refinement is written INLINE, not through a `type` alias. A named alias
takes a different path on the *mut spine (checker_lower_named_type_mut does
not consult the refinement table) and fails with E008 "expected Fp, found
i64" long before the refinement is consulted -- a separate, unfixed defect
that this test deliberately does not depend on.
